extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and patent prosecutors (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on when and how to prepare and file Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs) with the USPTO during U.S. patent prosecution, including timing windows, required statements/fees, form usage, common mistakes, and verification steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information (37 C.F.R. § 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. patent law, inventors and those associated with filing or prosecuting patent applications have a duty to disclose to the USPTO all known prior art or other information that may be 'material' in determining patentability; this duty continues until a patent has issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is satisfied when 'material' information is submitted to the USPTO in an IDS. There is no duty to perform a search, but failure to disclose material information may render an issued patent unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality — rule of thumb for what to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no absolute rule for what information is 'material,' but a good rule of thumb is to disclose all information that is relevant to the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of material information include related U.S. patent applications and patents of the applicant and references cited in a PCT or foreign counterpart application. When in doubt, disclose—better to err on the side of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for IDS consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: For information in an IDS to be officially considered during the pendency of an application, the IDS must be timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File IDSs (and supplemental IDSs) as early as possible to ensure Examiner consideration and to avoid additional costs. In some cases an RCE may be required solely to have an IDS considered. Untimely IDSs may not be considered and can have adverse effects on prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Stage filing window — 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file an IDS within 3 months of the U.S. filing date, or before the mailing of a first office action on the merits or after the filing of a Request for Continued Examination (RCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS is filed during this 'First Stage' there is no need to file a 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) statement and no government fee is required with the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Stage filing window — 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the First Stage has expired, an applicant may file an IDS before the mailing of a final Office action, a Notice of Allowance, or an Ex parte Quayle action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed in this 'Second Stage' must be accompanied by either a 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) statement or the government fee set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 1.17(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of a 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1.97(e) statement must state either (1) that each item was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the IDS; or (2) that no item was cited in such a communication and, after reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than three months prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is used in the Second and Third Stage to avoid payment of the government fee; the second alternative requires a 'reasonable inquiry' by the signer regarding knowledge by designated individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Stage filing window — 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Second Stage has expired, an applicant may file an IDS before or with payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed in this 'Third Stage' must be accompanied by both a 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) statement and the government fee set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 1.17(p). If a 1.97(e) statement cannot be made at this stage, the applicant must file an RCE to have the IDS considered by the Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file an IDS (form and procedural additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS can be filed with the USPTO using form PTO/SB/08a; further instructions are available at the USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transmittal letter may be filed with the IDS to briefly explain compliance with USPTO rules and to include additional statements (for example, a statement under 37 C.F.R. § 1.704(d)). Follow the USPTO instructions for preparing PTO/SB/08a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter usage and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal letter filed with the IDS can be useful to explain why the submission complies with USPTO rules and to include additional statements regarding the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the letter to clarify compliance and to include any optional regulatory statements (e.g., under 37 C.F.R. § 1.704(d)) that might help the Examiner process the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes to avoid when preparing and filing IDSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent filing errors can cause an IDS to be non-compliant and thus not considered by the Examiner; several common mistakes are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid: failing to submit copies of foreign references and non-patent literature with an IDS; failing to resubmit a corrected IDS (a non-compliant IDS typically will not be considered and will simply be placed in the file); failing to submit an IDS with references mentioned in the body of the application (only references cited in an IDS are required to be considered); citing immaterial or cumulative references (which increases time and possible government fees); not staying up-to-date on IDS requirements; failing to submit supplemental IDSs after discovery of previously unknown prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Examiner consideration before paying issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should verify that each reference submitted in an IDS has been considered by the Examiner before payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Examiner is required to sign each IDS that he/she considered during prosecution; applicants can check the file wrapper in the USPTO's PAIR system and confirm the Examiner's signature on each submitted IDS indicating that the cited references have been considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and strategic recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to satisfy the duty to disclose material information can have severe consequences; strategically, IDS timing and completeness matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because failure to disclose material information can render a patent unenforceable, applicants are encouraged to consider when and whether to file IDSs based on each application's particular circumstances and to verify disclosure requirements according to current USPTO rules and regulations.
